MGIMS Sevagram Organises a Grand Walkathon on World Heart Day
Monday, 29 September 2025
1815 Hits
Sevagram, Sept 28: The Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, organized a grand Walkathon on the occasion of World Heart Day with the theme “Pulse: Walk/Run for Every Beat.” The event drew an overwhelming response with over 550 registrations from across different age groups.
Participants included students, faculty, residents, staff, nurses, and citizens from outside the campus. The Walkathon also saw participation across generations, with the youngest walker being 7 years old and the oldest 75 years old. Flagged off from the Kasturba Vidya Mandir Ground, MGIMS Campus, the Walkathon offered 3 km, 5 km, and 10 km options up to Karanji Kaji village. Participants carried placards and slogans encouraging the community to adopt simple lifestyle habits that strengthen heart health.
To ensure smooth conduct, refreshment and aid checkpoints were set up at regular intervals, while an ambulance with doctors was stationed on the route. Free T-shirts and caps were given to registrants, while finishers received medals—bronze (3 km), silver (5 km), and gold (10 km).
“Our goal was to create awareness about heart health through a simple yet powerful activity like walking,” said Dr. Preetam Salunkhe, Associate Professor of Medicine, MGIMS, and a core organiser of the event. “The turnout and energy of the participants were beyond our expectations,” added Dr. Abhishek Raut, Professor of Community Medicine, MGIMS.
A participant summed it up saying, “It was both fun and meaningful to walk together for a cause.”
The Walkathon highlighted MGIMS’s commitment to promoting preventive health and creating awareness amongst the community.
